review_notes: Reviewed all 119 lines, the imported graph definitions, and the uses of these measurability lemmas in NoCollisionExtension. The only well-supported specialization I found is the real-valued, ℕ-indexed injectivity measurability theorem. The proposed generalization follows the existing proof pattern; I have not compiled the replacement.

findings.excerpt:
theorem measurable_injective_labels :
    Measurable (fun U : ℕ → ℝ => Function.Injective U) := by
  exact Measurable.forall (fun u => Measurable.forall (fun v =>
    ((measurable_pi_apply u).eq (measurable_pi_apply v)).imp measurable_const))
findings.problem: The proof only uses measurability of equality between label values, but the statement fixes labels to ℝ and indices to ℕ. This limits reuse for other measurable label spaces and countable index types.
findings.proposed_change: Generalize to `theorem measurable_injective_labels {ι β : Type*} [Countable ι] [MeasurableSpace β] [MeasurableEq β] : Measurable (fun U : ι → β => Function.Injective U) := by exact Measurable.forall (fun u => Measurable.forall (fun v => ((measurable_pi_apply u).eq (measurable_pi_apply v)).imp measurable_const))`. The existing proof uses precisely this pairwise-equality argument; `MeasurableEq β` supplies measurable equality, and countability supplies the measurable universal quantifiers. This also covers the empty-index case, where injectivity is vacuous.
findings.benefit: Makes the reusable measurability result available for non-real labels and other countable vertex types, while retaining the current ℕ-to-ℝ application when its measurable-equality instance is available.
